title: Depressive episode with mood-congruent delusions/hallucinations: major depressive disorder with psychotic features
topic: Major depressive disorder with psychotic features
vignette: A 45-year-old man is hospitalized due to suicidal ideation. Over the past month, the patient has become increasingly depressed, withdrawn, and physically restless. He has had increasing difficulty concentrating at his job as a computer programmer. The patient's appetite has been poor, and he has had difficulty falling and staying asleep. He stopped going to work last week and refused to leave the house until his hospitalization. The patient has no medical or psychiatric history. Physical examination is unremarkable apart from a 4.5-kg (10-lb) weight loss. On mental status examination, the patient appears depressed and anxious. He reports that he is responsible for "all the evil in the world" and has heard a voice for the past week telling him that he does not deserve to live. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

clues.text: increasingly depressed, withdrawn, and physically restless
clues.note: A sustained depressed mood with psychomotor change over a month meets the core of a major depressive episode.
Insomnia, plus poor concentration, poor appetite/weight loss, and suicidal ideation, fulfills the neurovegetative criteria (SIG E CAPS) for major depressive disorder.

clues.text: responsible for "all the evil in the world"
clues.note: A delusion of guilt/worthlessness that is MOOD-CONGRUENT (thematically consistent with depression) indicates psychotic features arising within the depressive episode.

clues.text: heard a voice for the past week telling him that he does not deserve to live
clues.note: An auditory hallucination occurring DURING the depressive episode (not independently) defines major depression WITH psychotic features.

whatMatters: A full major depressive episode (>=2 weeks of depressed mood + neurovegetative symptoms + suicidal ideation) with psychotic symptoms - MOOD-CONGRUENT delusions of guilt and auditory hallucinations - occurring ONLY during the mood episode = MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER WITH PSYCHOTIC FEATURES. Answer C.
strategy: Confirm a major depressive episode, then note the psychosis occurs exclusively during the mood episode and is mood-congruent -> MDD with psychotic features. Reject bipolar (no mania/hypomania history), delusional disorder (isolated delusions without other psychotic symptoms or a full mood episode), schizoaffective disorder (requires psychosis for >=2 weeks WITHOUT prominent mood symptoms), and schizophrenia/schizophreniform (psychosis in the absence of a mood disorder, with duration criteria).

options.text: Major depressive disorder with psychotic features

eliminations.label: Bipolar with psychotic features - no mania/hypomania
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a mood disorder with at least one manic/hypomanic episode. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: there is no history of mania or hypomania (elevated mood, decreased need for sleep, grandiosity), so bipolar disorder is excluded. ✅ Correct if: a prior manic/hypomanic episode.

eliminations.label: Delusional disorder - isolated delusions, no full mood episode
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: >=1 month of delusions without other psychotic symptoms and with only brief/absent mood symptoms. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has hallucinations plus a full major depressive episode, not isolated delusions. ✅ Correct if: nonbizarre delusions alone with preserved functioning.

eliminations.label: Schizoaffective disorder - psychosis WITHOUT mood symptoms >=2 wk
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: mood episodes PLUS psychosis, but requires >=2 weeks of delusions/hallucinations in the ABSENCE of a major mood episode. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: here the psychotic symptoms occur only DURING the depressive episode; no evidence of psychosis without mood symptoms. ✅ Correct if: >=2 weeks of psychosis without concurrent mood symptoms plus mood episodes.

eliminations.label: Schizophrenia - psychosis without a mood disorder
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: >=6 months of psychotic symptoms with functional decline, independent of mood. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the psychosis here is embedded in a mood episode and is mood-congruent, not a primary psychotic disorder. ✅ Correct if: chronic psychosis without a defining mood episode.

eliminations.label: Schizophreniform - psychotic disorder 1-6 months
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: schizophrenia-like psychosis lasting 1-6 months without a mood disorder. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the psychotic symptoms occur within a depressive episode, not as a standalone psychotic disorder. ✅ Correct if: 1-6 months of primary psychosis without a mood episode.

reasoning: The patient has a major depressive episode (depressed mood + neurovegetative symptoms + suicidal ideation over a month)
Psychotic symptoms (mood-congruent guilt delusion + auditory hallucination) occur DURING the episode
Psychosis confined to the mood episode = MDD with psychotic features (not a primary psychotic or schizoaffective disorder)
-> major depressive disorder with psychotic features; answer C
mechanism: MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER WITH PSYCHOTIC FEATURES is a severe subtype of unipolar depression in which PSYCHOTIC symptoms (delusions and/or hallucinations) occur EXCLUSIVELY during a MAJOR DEPRESSIVE EPISODE. This patient meets criteria for a major depressive episode - >=2 weeks of depressed mood plus several neurovegetative symptoms (impaired concentration, poor appetite with weight loss, insomnia, psychomotor changes) and SUICIDAL IDEATION. His psychotic symptoms are MOOD-CONGRUENT (thematically depressive): a delusion of being responsible for 'all the evil in the world' (guilt/worthlessness) and an auditory hallucination telling him he doesn't deserve to live. Because the psychosis is present only during the mood episode, the diagnosis is MDD with psychotic features (which requires combined ANTIDEPRESSANT + ANTIPSYCHOTIC therapy, or electroconvulsive therapy). It is distinguished from SCHIZOAFFECTIVE DISORDER, which requires >=2 weeks of psychosis in the ABSENCE of a major mood episode, and from primary psychotic disorders (schizophrenia, schizophreniform) that occur without a defining mood episode; bipolar disorder is excluded by the absence of mania/hypomania. (This is a sensitive topic involving suicidal ideation; if this resonates personally, please know support is available and I can help you find appropriate resources.)

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Psych > MDD with psychotic features: major depressive episode + psychosis only during the episode; often mood-congruent (guilt, worthlessness, nihilism); treat with antidepressant + antipsychotic or ECT; distinguish from schizoaffective (psychosis without mood >=2 wk).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Full depressive episode + psychosis confined to it = MDD with psychotic features.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on major depressive episode (SIG E CAPS), mood-congruent psychosis, schizoaffective criteria, or delusional disorder? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Schizoaffective needs psychosis WITHOUT mood >=2 wk; schizophrenia/schizophreniform = psychosis without a mood episode; bipolar needs mania; delusional = isolated delusions.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: psychosis only during a depressive episode = MDD with psychotic features (treat with antidepressant + antipsychotic or ECT).

keywords.front: Psychosis only during a depressive episode

keywords.back: >=2 weeks of psychosis WITHOUT a major mood episode
SIG E CAPS (sleep, interest, guilt, energy, concentration, appetite, psychomotor, suicidality)

firstAid.detail: Psych: depressive episode + mood-congruent psychosis confined to it.
Psych > schizoaffective, schizophrenia, delusional, bipolar distinctions.
Psych > combined therapy for psychotic depression.

memoryHook: When the depression itself talks - guilt delusions and a voice saying he doesn't deserve to live, only during the low mood - it's depression WITH psychotic features, not a separate psychotic illness.
